how_read: scripts/kb/fetch_wiki_live_pages.py --api https://cyberpunk.fandom.com/api.php --titles <pages> (page text as rendered by the wiki, link markup removed; the pages are kept in build/wiki-live/cyberpunk-fandom/). Every quoted passage below was checked, by script, to appear word for word in the page text read at the revision named (table markers removed, white space collapsed). The wiki also covers the tabletop games and the anime; every page used here describes the video game, and a line states a video-game fact only where the page says so for Cyberpunk 2077. Where a page marks something as needing verification, or mentions an ending or a late quest, the note leaves it out.

lines.line: Summary: Arasaka arm cyberware for fighting up close with swift, deadly slashes. It deals Physical damage and has a 10-20% chance to make enemies bleed.

quoted: Mantis Blades allow you to slice and dice your enemies with swift, deadly slashes.
Deal Physical damage. 10-20% Bleeding chance
The Daikon NT Mantis Blades are manufactured by Arasaka.

lines.line: Uses: Close-range melee. While you use them you can leap at an enemy within range to deal massive damage, and every point of Reflexes adds 0.5% damage with them. The game counts them as bladed weapons, which the wiki calls perfect for assassination and stealth executions.

quoted: While using the Mantis Blades, you can leap to enemies within range to deal massive damage.
Reflexes Attuned +0.5% damage with this cyberware per Attribute Point.
Bladed weapons are sharp, fast, and deadly. Perfect for assassination and stealth executions. Bladed weapons include Katanas, Machetes, and the Mantis Blades.

lines.line: Tips: Any Ripperdoc sells them once you reach level 10, and the quality goes up every 10 levels. The Arms slot has room for only one piece of cyberware, so you choose between them and the other arm cyberware.

quoted: Can be purchased from any Ripperdoc after reaching level 10. Quality increases every 10 levels.
Arms (1 slot)

lines.line: Summary: Arm cyberware that lets you whip several enemies at once from a distance. It deals Physical damage with a 10-20% chance to make enemies bleed.

quoted: Monowire is arm replacement cyberware that allows you to whip multiple enemies at once from a distance.
Deal Physical damage. 10-20% Bleeding chance

lines.line: Uses: Melee and short-range fighting. It has a quickhack slot that starts empty: once you have the Jailbreak Relic perk you can put a Control quickhack in it, and the quickhack is uploaded to anything hit by a charged attack. Every point of Intelligence adds 0.5% damage with it.

quoted: This implant allows you to deal more Physical damage in melee combat and short ranged combat.
Empty Quickhack Slot
If the Jailbreak Relic perk has been obtained, the Monowire can be modified with a Control Quickhack. This quickhack will be uploaded to targets that are hit with a charged attack.
Intelligence Attuned +0.5% damage with this cyberware per Attribute Point.

lines.line: Tips: Any Ripperdoc sells it once you reach level 10, and the quality goes up every 10 levels, up to Tier 5. The Arms slot has room for only one piece of cyberware, so you choose between it and the other arm cyberware.

quoted: Can be purchased from any Ripperdoc after reaching level 10. Quality increases every 10 levels, up to Tier 5.
Arms (1 slot)

lines.line: Summary: Arasaka arm cyberware that launches an explosive projectile for massive Physical damage.

quoted: Launches an explosive projectile that deals massive Physical damage.
Mfr. Arasaka

lines.line: Uses: Aiming and launching an explosive projectile. A charged shot gains +30% damage, +25% explosion radius and +40% dismemberment chance. Every point of Technical Ability adds 0.5% damage with it.

quoted: This implant allows you to aim and launch an explosive projectile that deals massive Physical damage.
Charged shots gain: +30% damage +25% explosion radius +40% dismemberment chance
Technical Ability Attuned +0.5% damage with this cyberware per Attribute Point.

lines.line: Tips: Any Ripperdoc sells it once you reach level 10, and the quality goes up every 5 levels. The Arms slot has room for only one piece of cyberware, so you choose between it and the other arm cyberware.

quoted: Can be purchased from any Ripperdoc after reaching level 10. Quality increases every 5 levels.
Arms (1 slot)

lines.line: Summary: Arasaka arm replacement cyberware that is lightweight, efficient and hard-hitting. It deals Physical damage with a 10-20% chance to make enemies bleed.

quoted: Gorilla Arms are lightweight, efficient and hard-hitting arm replacement cyberware.
Mfr. Arasaka
Deal Physical damage. 10-20% Bleeding chance

lines.line: Uses: Hard-hitting melee. Every point of Body adds 0.5% damage with them. The wiki's weapons page lists them with the blunt weapons, which it calls heavy, slow and non-lethal, with a chance to stun.

quoted: Body Attuned +0.5% damage with this cyberware per Attribute Point.
This implant allows you to deal more Physical damage in melee combat, and have a 10-20% chance to apply a Bleed effect.

Blunt weapons are heavy, slow and non-lethal. They employ brute force and have a chance to stun their opponents. Blunt weapons include Hammers, One and Two-Handed Clubs, Gorilla Arms, and unarmed/bare fists.

lines.line: Tips: Any Ripperdoc sells them once you reach level 10, and the quality goes up every 10 levels. The Arms slot has room for only one piece of cyberware, so you choose between them and the other arm cyberware.

quoted: Can be purchased from any Ripperdoc after reaching level 10. Quality increases every 10 levels.
Arms (1 slot)

lines.line: Summary: Guns that fire guided rounds which lock on to targets and seek them out. They are one of the three gun types, alongside Power and Tech, and they only aim themselves if you have a Smart Link implant.

quoted: Guns are classified as either Power, Smart, or Tech
Smart weapons aim for the wielder by using smart rounds that lock on and seek out their targets, though they need to be within the weapons's tracking box.
The Smart Link cyberware is required to enable smart-targeting

lines.line: Uses: Letting rounds seek out targets inside the weapon's tracking box. The rounds can curve around obstacles to reach their target, but they travel slower than ordinary bullets and hits are not always guaranteed. Smart Link is Hands cyberware, and a better Smart Link tracks better; from Tier 3 up it also lengthens target-lock duration by 10-20% and adds 5-15% crit damage with Smart weapons.

quoted: Smart bullets can curve around obstacles to hit their target, but travel slower than conventional rounds.
with better quality Smart Links improving the tracking ability of the gun, as hits are not always guaranteed.
The Smart Link is Cyberware for the Hands in Cyberpunk 2077.
At Tier 3 and above it will increase target-lock duration by 10-20% and Crit Damage with Smart Weapons by 5-15%.

lines.line: Tips: Tyger Claws gangers have Masking Ink in their tattoos, which gives them a 50% chance to make smart projectiles miss. The Ping quickhack, from Tier 3, adds 25% lock-on speed with Smart weapons against pinged enemies.

quoted: Members of the Tyger Claws gang use Masking Ink in their tattoos that jams the smart-targeting ability, giving them a 50% chance to cause smart projectiles to miss.
Tier 3 +25% lock-on speed with Smart weapons against Pinged enemies.

lines.line: Summary: Guns that use railgun technology, firing projectiles driven by an electromagnetic charge. They are one of the three gun types, alongside Power and Smart. They give up rate of fire for penetrating power, which depends on how long you hold the charge.

quoted: Guns are classified as either Power, Smart, or Tech

Tech weapons are weapons that use railgun technology, firing projectiles that are propelled with an electromagnetic charge. What they give up in terms of rate of fire they make up for in penetrating power, depending on how long the charge is held.

lines.line: Uses: Shooting through obstacles, because a charged shot can penetrate them. Perks for Tech weapons are in the Technical Ability attribute, and using them earns experience in the Engineer skill.

quoted: Tech weapons can be charged to fire a bullet capable of penetrating obstacles.
Perks specifically applying to Tech weapons can be found in the Technical Ability Attribute, and utilizing Tech weapons grants experience for the Engineer skill.

lines.line: Tips: A Tech weapon cannot take a suppressor, though most accept a custom sight. They use caseless ammunition, typically jacketed steel flechette.

quoted: Tech weapons cannot be fitted with a suppressor, but most of them accept a custom sight.
These weapons use caseless ammunition, typically jacketed steel flechette.

lines.line: Summary: The datashard you install in your Neuroport that lets you use quickhacks and Breach Protocol. Breach Protocol cannot be used at all without one.

quoted: cyberdecks have evolved to be a type of datashard that is installed in one's Neuroport system, and allows its users to perform Netrunner abilities, such as quickhacks and Breach Protocol.
thus a cyberdeck is mandatory in order to make use of Breach Protocol.

lines.line: Uses: Each deck has base RAM that quickhacks spend, a buffer size that sets how many characters you can pick from the Code Matrix in Breach Protocol, and slots for extra quickhacks. It comes with some device quickhacks already installed, and which ones depends on the maker and rises with quality.

quoted: In order to perform quickhacks, you require base RAM.
The buffer size is used during Breach Protocol, and determines the amount of characters you can select from the Code Matrix.
Every cyberdeck allows for the installation of an additional quickhack.
The type and amount of preinstalled device quickhacks varies per manufacturer and increases at higher quality.

lines.line: Tips: A spent unit of RAM takes 60 seconds outside of combat to come back. Quickhacking perks in the Intelligence attribute and Frontal Cortex cyberware can change how much RAM you have, a higher quality deck gives a bigger buffer, and some enemies resist quickhacks, which raises the RAM needed to hack them.

quoted: Once a RAM unit has been used, it will take 60 seconds outside of combat to recover.
can be modified by perks in the Quickhacking skill tree in the Intelligence attribute or by installing Frontal Cortex cyberware.
The buffer size can be increased by equipping higher quality cyberdecks.
Certain enemies may have quickhack resistance, increasing the amount of base RAM required for them to be hacked.

lines.line: Summary: Two healing consumables. The MaxDoc is a Trauma Team inhaler that instantly restores 50-126 Health. The Bounce Back is an injector that instantly restores 10-30 Health, then regenerates 6-17 Health per second for 10 seconds.

quoted: The MaxDoc is an inhaler manufactured by Trauma Team.
It allows the user to restore 50-126 Health when used.
The Bounce Back allows the user to instantly restore 10-30 Health, and then regenerating an additional 6-17 Health per second for 10 seconds.
Type Injector

lines.line: Uses: Restoring Health. The MaxDoc is one instant burst, while the Bounce Back is a smaller burst followed by 10 seconds of regeneration. A Bounce Back upgrades itself automatically when you pick up a higher quality one.

quoted: Instantly restores 50-126 Health.
Item will be upgraded automatically when acquiring a higher quality.

lines.line: Tips: Both turn up in caches and on enemies. Vendors sell the MaxDoc and Meds Vendors sell the Bounce Back. A stack of consumables holds up to 150 in your inventory.

quoted: Can be acquired from caches, Enemies, and Vendors.
Can be acquired from caches, Enemies, and Meds Vendors.
These items have a max stack of 150 in your inventory

sections.name: Enemies with Kerenzikov or a Sandevistan

lines.line: Summary: Some enemies carry reflex boosters. Kerenzikov lets an enemy dodge incoming projectiles. A Sandevistan lets an enemy move with lightning speed, avoid your bullets and close in quickly for melee, and it comes in Mk.1, Mk.2 and Mk.3 versions.

quoted: A classic and widely-used reflex booster that allows enemies to dodge incoming projectiles.
This classic implant allows the enemy to move with lightning speed, avoiding your incoming bullets and closing in on you surprisingly quickly to engage in melee combat.
Sandevistan Mk.1
Sandevistan Mk.2
Sandevistan Mk.3

lines.line: Weak points: Against Kerenzikov, switch to melee and use a shotgun or a blade. Against the Mk.1 Sandevistan, finish the fight as fast as you can. The Cripple Movement quickhack disables an enemy's movement and the cyberware that supports movement and dodging.

quoted: When an enemy uses Kerenzikov, it's better to switch to melee combat, using a shotgun or blade.
When someone uses this Sandevistan model, it's best to try to finish the fight as fast as you can.
Cripple Movement 3 →4 → 6 12 0.3 - Disables enemy movement and cyberware that supports movement and dodging.

lines.line: Tips: The Wraiths' Revenant, a fast melee enemy, has Kerenzikov and a Mk.1 Sandevistan, and a Kang Tao sniper has a Sandevistan. The wiki says a Mk.2 means you are in deep trouble, and it words the Mk.3 even more strongly.

quoted: Fast Melee
Sandevistan Mk.1
Kerenzikov
Type Fast Sniper
Sandevistan
When someone uses this Sandevistan model, you're in deep trouble.
When someone uses this Sandevistan model, you're in deep shit.

lines.line: Summary: Enemy netrunners fight with quickhacks instead of guns. The Voodoo Boys Netrunner is a Tier 2 rare enemy that uses the Cyberware Malfunction, Reboot Optics, Ping and Overheat quickhacks, and it also carries EMP grenades.

quoted: The Netrunner is a Tier 2 enemy affiliated with the Voodoo Boys in Cyberpunk 2077.
Rarity Rare
A skilled enemy netrunner can use a variety of quickhacks* against you, and they won't hesitate.
*Uses the Cyberware Malfunction, Reboot Optics and Ping quickhacks.
Overheat A dangerous quickhack that directly attacks your nervous system
EMP Grenades The enemy is equipped with EMP grenades

lines.line: Weak points: EMP grenades deal bonus damage against enemy netrunners, and also against drones, mechs, robots and turrets.

quoted: EMP Grenade - Applies an EMP effect for 5 sec. - Deals bonus damage against enemy netrunners, drones, mechs, robots and turrets.

lines.line: Tips: Overheat makes your body temperature skyrocket and overheats your neural and cybernetic components, and it can also result in combustion. Enemy netrunners can drop quickhacks, and this one's drops include Tier 2 to Tier 5 quickhack components.

quoted: making your body temperature skyrocket and overheating your neural and cybernetic components. Can also result in combustion.
6-8 Tier 2 Quickhack Components
1 Tier 5 Quickhack Components
They can also drop from enemy netrunners or looted from Airdrops.

lines.line: Summary: Robots, mechs and drones are enemies you can only destroy. Human enemies can be taken down both lethally and non-lethally, but these cannot.

quoted: human enemies can be taken down both lethally or non-lethally, while robots, mechs, and drones can only be destroyed.

lines.line: Weak points: The Short Circuit quickhack deals extra damage to mechs, robots, drones and turrets, and EMP grenades deal bonus damage against drones, mechs, robots and turrets. The Detonate Grenade quickhack can also detonate their weakspots.

quoted: Short Circuit 3 →4 → 5 → 7 → 10 1.5 → 1 → 0.5 - Deals Damage. Mechs, Robots, drones and turrets receive additional damage.
Can also detonate weakspots on robots, drones, mechs and turrets.
Deals bonus damage against enemy netrunners, drones, mechs, robots and turrets.

lines.line: Tips: The Contagion quickhack is ineffective against mechs, robots, drones and turrets. An EMP grenade also disables turrets for as long as its effect lasts.

quoted: Ineffective against mechs, robots, drones and turrets.
Disables turrets for the duration of the EMP grenade effect.

lines.line: Summary: A big Japantown gang that prefers melee weapons, especially ceramic tantos and katanas, with pistols and cheap, unreliable submachine guns as backup. Their tattoos are fortified with microchips to confuse targeting systems.

quoted: The Tyger Claws prefer melee weapons, especially ceramic tantos and katanas
They also pack pistols and submachine guns, the latter usually cheap, plastic, multi-colored and unreliable.
luminous tattoos of Japanese demons fortified with microchips to confuse targeting systems.

lines.line: Weak points: The Hunter, a melee fighter, is a Tier 2 enemy with Weak rarity. Their Masking Ink tattoos give them a 50% chance to cause each Smart weapon projectile to miss.

quoted: The Hunter is a Tier 2 enemy affiliated with the Tyger Claws in Cyberpunk 2077.
Type Melee
Rarity Weak
50% Chance to not be hit by Smart Weapon projectiles.
giving them a 50% chance to cause smart projectiles to miss.

lines.line: Looks like: Luminous tattoos of Japanese demons, katanas and fast street bikes.

quoted: Tyger foot soldiers were easily recognized by their Asian luminous tattoos, fast street bikes, katanas, and tantos.
luminous tattoos of Japanese demons

lines.line: Tips: A Hunter has Break Hold, which makes it nigh-impossible to grab from behind. The gang's cyberware includes reflex boosters, augmented cyberlimbs and pain editors.

quoted: it'll be nigh-impossible to grab this enemy from behind.
Cyberware used by the gang included reflex boosters, augmented cyberlimbs, pain editors, and electronic countermeasures (ECM) systems disguised as tattoos.

lines.line: Summary: A gang that controls Watson and the Northside Industrial District, made up of people with heavy cyberware. Its Goon is a Tier 2 enemy of Weak rarity that can be a ranged or a melee fighter, and its Ironstormer is a Tier 2 heavy ranged enemy.

quoted: A gang that controls the districts of Watson and the Northside Industrial District (NID).
Their physical appearance was distinguished by their dehumanizing heavy cyberware augmentations and occult-inspired tattoos.
The Goon is a Tier 2 enemy affiliated with Maelstrom in Cyberpunk 2077.
Rarity Weak
The Goon can either be a Ranged or a Melee enemy.
Type Heavy Ranged
The Ironstormer is a Tier 2 enemy affiliated with Maelstrom in Cyberpunk 2077.

lines.line: Weak points: The Goon has Weak rarity, while the Ironstormer is rated Rare and wears Medium Subdermal Armor, which increases its Health by 33% and Armor by 100%, and the wiki says an enemy in subdermal armor is much more difficult to throw off balance.

quoted: Rarity Weak
Rarity Rare
Increases Health by 33% and Armor by 100%.
An enemy with subdermal armor is more resistant to damage and is much more difficult to throw off balance.

lines.line: Looks like: Intimidating faceplates and hostile optic implants, and goggle-like cybereyes that glow a ghastly red.

quoted: You can easily recognize them by their intimidating faceplates and hostile optic implants
Maelstrom members often implant goggle-like cybereyes that glow a ghastly red

lines.line: Tips: Goons and Ironstormers have Smokey Eye, so they can see you clearly through smoke, and the ranged ones throw frag grenades that can tear you to shreds if you stand in the blast. Members are also fond of mantis blade implants in their lower arms.

quoted: Smokey Eye The enemy can see you clearly through clouds of smoke.
Frag Grenades The enemy is equipped with a classic shrapnel grenade. Don't underestimate them – if you find yourself within their blast radius, the shrapnel can tear you to shreds.
Smokey Eye The enemy can see you clearly through clouds of smoke.
Frag Grenades The enemy is equipped with a classic shrapnel grenade.
Maelstrom members are also fond of lower arm mantis blade implants

lines.line: Summary: Loosely linked gangs that kidnap people and forcibly harvest their cyberware. They are all over Night City, thickest in northern Pacifica and the southern part of Wellsprings. Their Vulture is a Tier 2 heavy ranged enemy with frag grenades.

quoted: They are known for kidnapping people and forcibly harvesting their cyberware.
Scavengers can be found all over Night City.
they have a more concentrated presence in northern Pacifica and southern part of Wellsprings.
The Vulture is a Tier 2 enemy affiliated with the Scavengers in Cyberpunk 2077.
Type Heavy Ranged
Frag Grenades

lines.line: Weak points: The wiki rates the gang's threat level as Medium in 2077, and its groups are small bands with little or no internal structure. The Vulture wears Medium Subdermal Armor, which increases its Health by 33% and Armor by 100%.

quoted: Threat Level Medium (2077)
they tend to form small bands with little or no internal hierarchy or structure
Increases Health by 33% and Armor by 100%.

lines.line: Looks like: Tracksuits, Soviet cyberware and criminal tattoos.

quoted: Scavengers are recognized by their tracksuits, Soviet cyberware, and criminal tattoos.

lines.line: Tips: Their cyberware includes cyberoptics, pain editors, health monitors and Kerenzikov, which lets an enemy dodge incoming projectiles. A Vulture can also leap with Charge Jump.

quoted: Cyberware used by the gang include cyberoptics, pain editors, health monitors, Kerenzikov, and K.E.R.S.
A classic and widely-used reflex booster that allows enemies to dodge incoming projectiles.
Charge Jump Cybermodified leg joints and reinforced, advanced muscle kinetics allow the enemy to traverse large distances with quick, high jumps.

lines.line: Summary: The NCPD's elite unit for hunting cyberpsychos. If you commit crimes until your wanted rating reaches five stars, MaxTac officers are sent after you, the last enemy type to hunt you while you are wanted. They work in squads of four, and on higher difficulties they can kill you in just a few shots whatever your level.

quoted: MaxTac is an elite, special ops division of the NCPD with a singular aim: eliminate cyberpsychos.
reaching a maximum wanted rating (five stars) will result in the deployment MaxTac officers, who serve as the final enemy type to hunt V down while wanted.
On higher difficulties, they are capable of killing V in just a few shots regardless of character level.
MaxTac officers operate in squads of four each

lines.line: Weak points: A squad's netrunner avoids direct combat, and the quickhacks it favours are slow to upload. The Mantis operator, who fights up close with MaxTac-built mantis blades, has the second highest armor rating.

quoted: Netrunner - Field hackers who typically avoid direct combat in favor of utilizing quickhacks that are slow to upload, but cause high amounts of damage.
Mantis - Close-quarter specialists who utilize MaxTac-built mantis blades and the Omaha as backup weapons. They hold the second highest armor rating.

lines.line: Tips: The roles are Assault (Ajax and Defender), Mantis, Heavy (a walking tank in an exosuit with the Defender), Netrunner and Sniper (Ashura, and a heavier use of Sandevistan). Officers regularly use Sandevistan Mk. 3 and Kerenzikov.

quoted: Assault - Frontline fighters who utilize the Ajax and Defender.
Heavy - Walking tanks in exosuits who utilize the Defender to dish out large amounts of damage in seconds.
Sniper - Long-range specialists armed with the Ashura to attack V from a distance. These officers make significantly more use of their Sandevistan.
For cyberware, officers make regular use of Sandevistan Mk. 3 and Kerenzikov.
